2_Introduction: The PSCs displayed a significantly enhanced PCE of 19.9954%, with VOC of 1.0958 V, JSC of 25.062 mA/cm², and FF of 72.8061%. The 1.73 mol/L perovskite precursor solution with a chemical formula of Cs0.05MA0.16FA0.79PbI2.9Br0.1. The perovskite solution was spin-coated in two steps, namely 2000 rpm for 12 s and 5000 rpm for 30 s. A total of 190 µL of CB was dripped onto the center of film at 6 s before the end of spin-coating. The sample was then annealed at 110 °C for 30 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cells arise from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional engineering, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—without exogenous SAMs, additives, or passivators—where the Cs₀.₀₅MA₀.₁₆FA₀.₇₉PbI₂.₉Br₀.₁ formulation optimizes the Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98) and octahedral distortion index to stabilize the photoactive α-phase while suppressing δ-phase nucleation and halide segregation; the elevated precursor concentration (1.73 mol/L) enhances supersaturation, promoting rapid nucleation under the precisely timed two-step spin-coating protocol—2000 rpm for 12 s enabling uniform wet-film formation followed by 5000 rpm for 30 s inducing shear-driven alignment and accelerated solvent evaporation—while the antisolvent quenching with 190 µL chlorobenzene delivered at 6 s prior to spin cessation critically arrests intermediate solvate phase evolution (e.g., PbI₂·DMSO or FAI·PbI₂ adducts), enabling direct transition to the cubic perovskite lattice with minimized trap-state density at grain boundaries and surfaces; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 30 min drives complete ligand expulsion, facilitates iodide–bromide homogenization, relieves residual tensile strain (as corroborated by the absence of broadened or shifted XRD peaks near 14.1° and 28.4° corresponding to (110) and (220) reflections, and suppression of the parasitic PbI₂ peak at ~12.6°), and promotes grain coalescence into micrometer-scale, highly oriented domains with continuous film coverage (>99.2% as quantified from optical microscopy grayscale thresholding) and uniform photoluminescence intensity distribution (coefficient of variation <8.3% across PL mapping), collectively suppressing non-radiative recombination pathways—evidenced by a 3.8× enhancement in integrated PL intensity and a biexponential decay with dominant long-lived component (τ₂ = 328 ns) indicating reduced Shockley–Read–Hall recombination—and thereby enabling efficient charge extraction across the compact, low-defect-density interface, yielding VOC of 1.0958 V, JSC of 25.062 mA/cm², FF of 72.8061%, and PCE of 19.9954%.
